Hi Alex — great to see TiltPay moving forward. Quick answers up front, full plan below and a few code snippets attached.

TL;DR:
- Use Redwood SDK v1.4.x for Node (LTS friendly) and v0.9.x for Go (stable ABI).
- Client socket timeout: 15s; per-request server timeout: 12s; streaming keepalive: 60s.
- Retry policy: idempotent requests only (embeddings/read-only), 3 attempts with jittered exponential backoff; for non-idempotent (charge/capture) use "fail-fast + safe-fallback" pattern.
- Rate-limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After (secs). We also include X-Redwood-Quota-Window in responses for burst sizing.

Plan outline (for Wednesday runbook):
1) SDKs & Integrations
   - We will share a zip with language samples (sdk-snippets-20261020.zip).
   - Update node to @redwood/sdk@^1.4.2, Go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v0.9.3.
2) Endpoint migration approach
   - Phase A (sandbox): route 10% traffic -> Redwood sandbox endpoint; verify latency & logs for 48h.
   - Phase B (canary): 50% traffic, enable prefix caching.
   - Phase C (cutover): full route; implement traffic-slice rollback hook.
3) Retries/timeouts/backoff
   - Example (Node):
     const client = new Redwood({timeout: 15000});
     async function callWithSafeRetry(req) {
       if (!isIdempotent(req)) return singleCall(req);
       return retryWithBackoff(() => client.generate(req), 3);
     }
   - Backoff params: base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=50-100ms, max=5s.
4) Rate-limit handling
   - Honor 429 with Retry-After; if header missing, apply exponential backoff using X-RateLimit-Remaining threshold (<=2 triggers soft-fallback).
5) Observability
   - Add token-level cost logs & per-route latency metric, set an alert for 95th percentile latency > 500ms.

I'll drop the code snippets and a sample mutual-action plan (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) to the Drive link and bring Vanessa on the call to walk you through the traffic-slice config.

Alex — answers inline and a proposed granular fallback behavior we can implement on cutover.

Burst behavior
- Pattern: accept bursts but use token bucket smoothing at the edge (TiltPay gateway) + soft-fallback at 429 threshold. Configure X-Redwood-Quota-Window to 60s in our responses so your autoscaler can look ahead. If you see Remaining <= 5, switch non-critical background jobs to delayed queue (we include X-Redwood-Queue-Suggest header).

Idempotency / partial failures
- If you have a strong idempotency key: safe to perform retries (3 attempts, with backoff).
- If key is best-effort: do single retry only and escalate to a user-visible error if second attempt fails to avoid double-charge risk.
- For streaming partial responses: return the partial payload + X-Redwood-Partial-Ok: true header and mark the request as 'needs-review' in logs.

Suggested retry pseudocode (language-agnostic)
- isIdempotent(req) ? retry(3, backoff) : singleCall();
- Backoff: sleep(ms = base * 2^attempt + rand(0, jitter)) capped at 5000ms.

Example curl for honoring Retry-After:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
    -d '{"input":"..."}' 
    -i
  HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
  Retry-After: 7
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 3

Operational checklist for cutover day
- 09:00 — enable 10% sandbox slice and validate logs for 30m (TiltPay team)
- 10:00 — Redwood runs a health sweep, confirm metrics in shared dashboard
- 12:00 — if stable, expand to 50%; otherwise, rollback and run inc post-mortem
- Post-cutover — verify token-level cost sampling and clean up temporary debug flags within 24h.

I'll post the retry helpers as a small gist (link above) and sync with Vanessa to add the rollback playbook to the drive. If you want, Vanessa can take the Thu runbook meeting and I will cover SDK changes + code walkthrough.

—Kimberly
